issues.description: Three proof postconditions call `Deref::deref` in specification context, which the supported Verus resolves as an illegal exec-mode call.
issues.rationale: The explicit method-call spelling resolves to executable `core::ops::deref::Deref::deref`, which cannot be called from a proof postcondition. All three locations share this mode-resolution root. The final repair replaces them with unary `*`, preserving the intended dereference properties in specification mode. The source blob is identical in the PR base and selected pre-repair commit, so this is an immediate pre-repair snapshot rather than a claim that the first PR commit introduced the defect.
issues.source_evidence: after/vstd_extra/src/manually_drop.rs: lines 34, 42, and 49 use explicit `.deref()` inside proof postconditions. Exact Verus c3014c7b reports `cannot call core::ops::deref::Deref::deref with mode exec` at line 34 and exits 101. Repair 501ef242 changes all three to unary dereference and reports `225 verified, 0 errors`.
issues.verification: Reproduced with Verus c3014c7b5df1e3d70eab4339f4b8fd26360e0499, Rust 1.85.1 and Z3 4.12.5: problem vstd_extra compilation exits 101 on exec-mode deref; repair exits 0 with 225 verified, 0 errors.
